audit.whatIsWrong: Ground Slam's attack-speed slow is sold purely as a defensive tool — "turning his crit DPS into wet noodles". Nothing connects it to Steel Tempest.
audit.why: Riot's own text says Steel Tempest "is treated as a basic attack and scales with all the same things", so attack speed lowers its effective cooldown. Ground Slam's attack-speed slow therefore does something far better than reduce his autos: it stretches the gap between Steel Tempest casts, which delays the two stacks he needs for the whirlwind knock-up, which in turn delays the airborne target Last Breath requires. One 7-second ability on your bar pushes back his entire combo chain, and the page never says so.
audit.corrected: The Ground Slam / Steel Tempest / knock-up / Last Breath chain stated in mid, whys[3] and spikes[1].
sources: champ-data/_kits/yasuo.json (Q "treated as a basic attack and scales with all the same things"; "At 2 stacks, Steel Tempest fires a whirlwind that knocks Airborne"; R "Blinks to an Airborne enemy champion")

audit.whatIsWrong: "Unstoppable Force ignores his Windwall and Q-knockup setup" states the right conclusion without the reason, and Wind Wall is never given a cooldown despite being the ability that decides your poke.
audit.why: Wind Wall blocks projectiles. Unstoppable Force is a dash, which is why it goes through — worth saying, because Seismic Shard genuinely IS a projectile and genuinely does get eaten, and a player who does not know the distinction will assume both are safe or both are not. The number that makes it playable: Wind Wall is 25 seconds at rank 1 and 17 at rank 5, and lasts 4. That is a 20-second window after every wall where your Q poke lands for free, and the page gives no such timer.
audit.corrected: Wall cooldowns and the projectile-versus-dash distinction added to early, mid, wants.foe[0] and whys[4].
sources: champ-data/_kits/yasuo.json (W "blocks all enemy projectiles for 4 seconds", cd 25/23/21/19/17)
champ-data/_kits/malphite.json (Q flagged projectile; R described as launching himself to a location)

audit.whatIsWrong: Sweeping Blade is called "his E dash" and treated as unlimited mobility. The restriction on it is never mentioned.
audit.why: Sweeping Blade "cannot be re-cast on the same enemy for a few seconds". Against you alone he gets one dash and then has to walk, so all of his in-and-out pressure is borrowed from the minion wave. That converts an abstract "respect his mobility" note into a wave-management instruction: a thin wave on your side of the lane is what strands him, and a big shoved wave is what lets him kite you forever. Nothing in the entry currently links his mobility to the wave at all.
audit.corrected: Added to early and wants.you; whys[2] rewritten around the same-target restriction.
sources: champ-data/_kits/yasuo.json (E "Cannot be re-cast on the same enemy for a few seconds")

audit.whatIsWrong: The chart reads Malphite / Skill / Yasuo / Yasuo / Malphite / Yasuo / Yasuo and contradicts the prose at three of the seven stages.
audit.why: win[0] says Malphite while whys[0] says "Yasuo's Q double-strike and E dash out-trade you at level 1" and spikes[0] labels Lvl 1-2 "Yasuo's window". win[3] says Yasuo while whys[3] and spikes[1] both say levels 4-5 are where "his crit DPS craters into your stacked armor". win[5] says Yasuo while whys[5] says the first armour item makes you "a genuine frontline his pre-IE crits can't break — force trades now". Only the last stage, where a full-crit Yasuo genuinely reclaims it, is labelled consistently.
audit.corrected: Yasuo / Skill / Yasuo / Malphite / Malphite / Malphite / Yasuo — matches every prose field and the 54.32% win rate over 1007 games.

audit.whatIsWrong: late says "his own R off your team's knockups makes him a teamfight monster".
audit.why: Backwards. Last Breath blinks to an airborne ENEMY champion, so an enemy Yasuo ults off HIS team's crowd control onto YOUR carries — your team's knock-ups do not feed him. It matters practically because it changes who you are protecting: the instruction should be about denying his team the setup and peeling your backline, not about your own team withholding CC. Worth pairing with the number, since Last Breath falls to 30 seconds at rank 3 while Unstoppable Force is still 100.
audit.corrected: late rewritten; the 30s-versus-100s ultimate gap added to spikes[3] and whys[6].
sources: champ-data/_kits/yasuo.json (R "Blinks to an Airborne enemy champion", cd 70/50/30)

edits.before: Yasuo's window: his Q double-strike and E dash out-poke you before W/E come online, so eat it and farm.
edits.after: Yasuo's window: Steel Tempest is a 4s poke and Wind Wall eats Seismic Shard, so eat it and farm.

edits.before: Once W (armor + AoE autos) and E (attack-speed slow) are up, his crit DPS craters into your stacked armor.
edits.after: Ground Slam's attack-speed slow stretches Steel Tempest's cooldown, delaying the knock-up his ult needs.

edits.before: Unstoppable Force ignores his Windwall and Q-knockup setup — R in, E to gut his attack speed, and you win the all-in.
edits.after: Wind Wall blocks projectiles; Unstoppable Force is a dash, so it goes through — R in, E his attack speed, win the all-in.

edits.before: His threat window: full-crit Yasuo with IE/Shieldbow + R off your knockups shreds even an armor-stacked frontline.
edits.after: His window: full-crit Yasuo, and Last Breath falls to 30s while your R is still 100s — he fights four times per your one.

edits.before: Reach Level 6 and use R as an unstoppable engage his Windwall and dash cannot answer
edits.after: Reach 6 and engage with R — it is a dash, so Wind Wall cannot block it like your Q

edits.before: Use E to slash his attack speed every trade, turning his crit DPS into wet noodles
edits.after: Ground Slam every trade — the attack-speed slow also stretches Steel Tempest's 4s

edits.before: Use Windwall to block your Q slow-bolt and deny your only ranged poke
edits.after: Wind Wall your Seismic Shard — 4 seconds of wall on a 25s cooldown

edits.before: Land his own R knockup off your engage and scale into a 2-item crit monster
edits.after: Ult off his own team's CC onto your carries and scale to 2-item crit

edits.before: Levels 1-3 are the only part of this lane that belongs to Yasuo. You have no trade pattern yet — Granite Shield is your only buffer and his Q double-strike plus E dash will out-poke you, so don't contest, just last-hit and let his flow shield pop on minions. Save your Q slow-bolt for when he actually commits, not to chuck across the wave where his Windwall can swallow it. Take the poke and know it does not matter once your armor turns on.
edits.after: Levels 1-3 are the only part of this lane that belongs to Yasuo. Granite Shield is your only buffer and Steel Tempest pokes every 4 seconds, so don't contest — last-hit and let his flow shield pop on minions. Save Seismic Shard for when he commits; thrown across the wave, Wind Wall simply swallows it for 4 seconds. Note too that Sweeping Blade cannot re-cast on the same target, so on a thin wave he gets one dash at you and then has to walk.

edits.before: Levels 4-6 flip the lane hard. W gives you bonus armor and AoE empowered autos while E slows his attack speed — that combination directly nullifies a crit auto-attacker, and his flow shield can't keep up with your sustain. At 6 your R is the trump card: it's an unstoppable dash, so it ignores his Q knockup setup and Windwall, and the moment you land it E craters his attack speed for the kill. Bait his E dash in, then E-W-Q him while his DPS is shut off.
edits.after: Levels 4-6 flip the lane hard, and Ground Slam is why. Steel Tempest is treated as a basic attack, so it scales with attack speed — slowing him stretches the gap between casts, delays the two stacks he needs for the whirlwind knock-up, and delays the airborne target Last Breath feeds on. At 6 your R is the trump card: Wind Wall blocks projectiles and your R is a dash, so it goes through what your Q cannot. Bait his Sweeping Blade in, then E-W-Q while his DPS is off.

edits.before: You own the mid-game frontline, but Yasuo is a hard scaler and the 2+ item window is his. Once he has IE or Shieldbow plus Infinity Edge crits, his sustained DPS starts cutting through even your stacked armor, and his own R off your team's knockups makes him a teamfight monster. Use your durability and R utility to peel and engage for your carries rather than dueling a fed Yasuo straight up — close the game on your mid-game lead before his crit items fully online.
edits.after: You own the mid-game frontline, but Yasuo is a hard scaler and the 2+ item window is his. With Infinity Edge his sustained DPS cuts through stacked armor, and Last Breath drops to 30 seconds while Unstoppable Force is still 100 — he gets four ultimates to your one. He blinks off HIS team's crowd control onto your carries, so the job is denying their setup and peeling, not withholding your own CC. Close on your mid-game lead before the crit items finish.

edits.before: Still his edge, but it's softening — bank your Granite Shield, save Q for a real commit, and farm through his flow shield.
edits.after: Still his edge, softening — bank Granite Shield, hold Seismic Shard for a commit so Wind Wall can't eat it, and farm.

edits.before: By level 3 it's even-ish: he can't all-in a shielded tank and you can't punish his mobility yet, so it's a skill standoff on the wave.
edits.after: Even-ish: Sweeping Blade can't re-cast on you, so on a thin wave he gets one dash and walks — the wave is what feeds his mobility.

edits.before: W's bonus armor and E's attack-speed slow come online — your stacked armor turns his crit autos into chip damage you out-sustain.
edits.after: Steel Tempest scales with attack speed, so Ground Slam's slow stretches its 4s cooldown and pushes back his knock-up combo.

edits.before: Unstoppable Force is your single biggest spike: it ignores his Windwall and knockup, and E guts his attack speed for the kill.
edits.after: Unstoppable Force is a dash, not a projectile — Wind Wall stops your Q and cannot stop your R. Land it, then E for the kill.

edits.before: Hard scaler reclaims it: full-crit Yasuo with IE/Shieldbow and R off knockups out-damages your armor — peel, don't duel.
edits.after: Hard scaler reclaims it: Last Breath hits 30s to your R's 100s, so he re-engages four times per commit — peel, don't duel.

notes: The kit file flags Malphite's R as a projectile. It is not one — the description is "launches himself to a location at high speed", which is a dash, and the flag is a tooltip-parsing artefact. This matters more here than anywhere else in the slice, because the whole level-6 argument rests on Wind Wall not stopping the R, so I stated the projectile-versus-dash reasoning explicitly rather than leaving it as an assertion. Same caveat as the Zac mirror on Malphite's Q and E "grounding" flags: artefacts of the words "through the ground" and "slams the ground", and I wrote nothing based on them. What I could NOT verify and left out: whether Wind Wall blocks Seismic Shard's slow application separately from its damage, and whether Malphite's knock-up on Yasuo can be cancelled by Sweeping Blade's dash — needsResearch is empty in both kits, which means unknown.
